stories.title: Far-Right AfD Achieves Significant Victory in Saxony-Anhalt State Election
stories.summary: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party secured a notable victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, receiving 44% of the vote, just shy of an absolute majority. This marks the most significant success for a far-right party in Germany since the Nazi era. Despite the win, the AfD fell three seats short of a majority and faces challenges in forming a government due to mainstream parties' refusal to collaborate with them. story_report.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt’s September 6 state election, the preliminary count put Alternative for Germany at 43.8% of second votes and 39 seats in the 83-member Landtag, three short of the 42 needed for an absolute majority. The result makes AfD the first far-right group to come close to regional power since World War II. Its leaders have begun seeking support to govern, but the CDU has reaffirmed it will not cooperate, leaving the formation of a government unsettled.

stories.title: Giorgia Meloni's Government Becomes Italy's Longest-Serving Since WWII
stories.summary: Giorgia Meloni's administration has surpassed 1,413 consecutive days in office, making it the longest-lasting government in Italy's postwar history. This milestone surpasses the previous record held by Silvio Berlusconi's second administration. Meloni, Italy's first female Prime Minister, has governed since 2022, navigating both domestic and international challenges.

story_report.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s cabinet reached 1,413 uninterrupted days in office on Sept. 3, 2026, overtaking Silvio Berlusconi’s 2001-05 administration as Italy’s longest-serving government since World War II. The milestone gives Meloni, Italy’s first woman to lead a government, a postwar durability record in a political system where cabinets have often changed before parliamentary terms end. Her administration has been in office since October 2022 and must continue to retain the confidence of both houses of Parliament.
